Calibration Every thermostat is calibrated before it leaves the factory. Under normal circumstances there will never be a need to recalibrate the thermostat again. To accommodate special needs, the thermostat may be recalibrated following these steps: 1. While holding the mode button in, press the fan button for 5 seconds. After all the icons in the display appear, release the buttons. 2. Press the Up and Down arrow buttons simultaneously, twice. 3. Press the up or down buttons until the flashing number equals the current room temperature. 4. Press the mode button to return to normal operation. Page 8

STEP #4 TEST OPERATION 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer Turn the power on to the Heating/Air Conditioning system. 6:03 Am Su 70 o COOL Press the MODE button repeatedly until Cooler 7M0ode Warmer the HEAT icon appears on the display. Press the Up or Down buttons until the set temperature is 10 degrees above room temperature. The furnace should turn on. 6:03 Am Su 70 o COOL Press the MODE button repeatedly until Cooler 7M0ode Warmer the COOL icon appears on the display. Press the Up or Down buttons until the set temperature is 10 degrees below room temperature. The air conditioner should turn on. NOTE: Most equipment has a time delay of 5 minutes between cool cycles. This feature is defeatable on the thermostat. Consult the Owner's Manual under Setup, cycles per hour. 6:03 Am Su 70 o COOL Press the MODE button to OFF. Press 70 Cooler Mode Warmer the FAN button to Fan On. The fan should turn on and run continuously. Page 9

TROUBLESHOOTING 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer SYMPTOM: When using 4 wires (R, G, W, Y), the air conditioning equipment tries repeatedly to turn on, but cannot. At times the display dims or disappears. CAUSE: There is not enough power available to "power share". REMEDY: Connect a 270 ohm, 10 watt power resistor at the furnace as shown below. For Problem A/C For Problem Heat RG W YC RG W YC TR300-10w TR300-10w 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer SYMPTOM: The air conditioning does not attempt to turn on. CAUSE: The compressor timer lockout may prevent the air conditioner from turning on, for a period of time. REMEDY: Consult the Owner's Manual in the Setup section to defeat the cycles per hour and compressor timeguard. 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer SYMPTOM: The display is blank. CAUSE: Lack of proper power. REMEDY: Make sure power is turned on to the furnace and 24vac between R & W. If C is used, 24vac between R & C. Page 10

TROUBLESHOOTING 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer SYMPTOM: The air conditioning does not attempt to turn on. CAUSE: The cooling setpoint is set too high. REMEDY: Consult the Owner's Manual in the Setup section to lower the cooling setpoint limit. 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer SYMPTOM: The heating does not attempt to turn on. CAUSE: The heating setpoint is set too low. REMEDY: Consult the Owner's Manual in the Setup section to raise the heating setpoint limit. Page 11

TROUBLESHOOTING 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer SYMPTOM: When controlling a residential heat pump, and asking for cooling, the heat comes on. CAUSE: Heat pump is not selected "on" in the Advanced Setup. REMEDY: Select heat pump on during Advanced Setup programming. Consult the Owner's Manual. 6:03 Am Su 70 Cooler Mode 70 o COOL Warmer SYMPTOM: When calling for cooling, both the heat and cool come on. CAUSE: The Advanced Setup is configured to control a heat pump, and the hvac the thermostat is controlling is a "conventional" (non heat pump) system. REMEDY: Consult the Owner's Manual in the Advanced Setup section to turn off the heat pump. 4Z95 Slimline P/N TSTAT0710 FCc Tested to Comply with FCC Standards FOR HOME OR OFFICE USE Page 12 P/N 88-416
